solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Protean spirit of record spinner in Islington area

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, spins records
N1 is the London postcode covering Islington, read here as the letters NI

explanation.surface: A shape-shifting soul belonging to a disc jockey who works around Islington.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a north London borough whose postcode is N1; the digit 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A djinni (genie) of Islamic lore is a spirit able to take many shapes, hence protean.

clue.text: Cabal originally taking over area after thirty days

indicators.note: after says the thirty-day month comes first, followed by the other letters
in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it

parts.note: June has thirty days; JUN is its abbreviation

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word taking

explanation.surface: A secret clique first seizing a district once a month has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letter of 'taking'; 'over' sets it above A in this down entry, and 'after' puts the pair after JUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A junta is a ruling clique, typically military, that has seized power: a political cabal.

clue.text: Directions devised, we hear, after athletic activity upset Nanny

indicators.note: after says the upset run comes first, followed by the directions and the rest
in a down clue, upset turns the word run upside down so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: a run is a piece of athletic activity
S and E, south and east, are compass directions

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word made is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: devised means made

explanation.surface: Instructions concocted, apparently, after some exercise upset the children's carer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RUN into NUR; 'we hear' gives MAID from MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after young children, which is what a nanny does.

clue.text: Girl employed in teaching riding

indicators.note: employed in says the answer is used within the run of letters of teaching riding

explanation.surface: A young woman working as a riding instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: The name straddles the two words: teachING RIDing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a female first name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: German bar inspiring Verdi's first operatic song

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the word ban takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to bar is to ban

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Verdi's

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A German pub prompting the opening of a Verdi opera's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb meaning prohibit; 'inspiring' (breathing in) is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bavarian comes from Bavaria, a state of southern Germany, so is a German.

clue.text: Doctor dealing with Banbury's charity event, possibly

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic doing business with an Oxfordshire town's people at a fundraising fete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the verb rearranging DEALING plus BANBURYS. Banbury is a market town in Oxfordshire, England; a bring-and-buy sale is a British fundraiser where people bring items to sell and buy others'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bring-and-buy sales are typically held to raise money for a charity, hence a charity event, possibly.

clue.text: Lively operatic prince feeding you in Paris

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the prince goes inside the French word

parts.note: vous is French for you
Prince Igor is the title role of Borodin's opera

explanation.surface: A spirited prince from opera dining with you in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The prince is the hero of Borodin's opera Prince Igor; 'feeding' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigorous means full of energy and strength, which is close to lively.

clue.text: Stick in the name of a sculptor

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Sticking a sculptor's name on something, perhaps a plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a verb but is the noun ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker, so his surname names a sculptor.

clue.text: Girl going to West London district for toughening

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
Ealing is a district of West London

explanation.surface: A young woman heading to Ealing to toughen up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a borough in west London, known for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing heats then slowly cools metal or glass to make it less brittle, a toughening process.

clue.text: Hatching a plot? Fascinating!

definitions.meaning: ... as the verb, scheming or plotting

explanation.surface: Someone scheming, and an onlooker's delighted exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the first sense as the verb form, conspiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue is to plot secretly; intriguing also means arousing keen interest, i.e. fascinating.

clue.text: Take courses at home in centre of Philadelphia

indicators.note: in places the home word within the middle pair
centre of picks the two middle letters of Philadelphia

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Studying at home somewhere in the middle of Philadelphia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' are meal courses, not classes; 'centre of' takes the two middle letters of the twelve-letter city, and 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To take courses, as in starter, main and dessert, is to eat a meal, i.e. to dine.

clue.text: Hesitating to own item of jewellery

parts.note: to have is to own
a ring is an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: Dithering over whether to buy a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: Havering is mainly British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver is chiefly British for dithering or vacillating, so havering is hesitating.

clue.text: Ready in Brazil to accept new tenant's first payment

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the Brazilian money holds the other letters

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and the real is the currency of Brazil

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of tenant's

explanation.surface: Cash in Brazil taken for a new tenant's initial payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready', short for ready money, is British slang for cash. 'to accept' puts N and T inside REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the sum paid to rent something, a regular payment.

clue.text: Young woman launching a festival

indicators.note: launching means starting off, so the young woman's word begins before a

parts.note: gal is informal for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A girl opening a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launching' sets GAL in front of A.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive social occasion, a kind of festival or celebration.

clue.text: Religious leader's Indian maid skirting coral reef

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge of, so the maid's word surrounds the reef

parts.note: an ayah is a nursemaid or maid in India
an atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef

explanation.surface: A cleric's Indian servant sailing round a coral reef.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'skirting' puts ATOLL inside AYAH.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shiite cleric in Iran, a religious leader.

clue.text: Obsessive knight, socially acceptable, wearing blue?

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the word for blue encloses the letter for acceptable

parts.note: blue can mean risqué or erotic
U means upper-class, so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A fixated knight, all very proper, dressed in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' is not a colour but racy, EROTIC; 'wearing' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurotic describes anxious, obsessive behaviour, so it fits obsessive.

clue.text: Primate telephoned by old sick aunt

parts.note: rang means telephoned

indicators.note: sick means unwell or out of order, so the letters of aunt are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ape getting a phone call from an elderly, poorly aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges AUNT into UTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, and so a primate.

clue.text: Nutter's constant stand on marijuana

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so the stand sits over the drug

parts.note: C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a rack is a stand for holding things
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A lunatic is forever standing up for cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person, which 'nutter' means in British slang.

clue.text: Light vehicle going around head of rare crustacean

parts.note: to light is to alight or land

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so the vehicle surrounds the letter

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of rare

explanation.surface: A lightweight car circling a rare crustacean's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is the verb, as a bird lights on a branch; 'going around' puts R inside CAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A land crab is a crab that lives mainly on land, a type of crustacean.

clue.text: Legendary vessel's slow movement leaving lake

indicators.note: leaving means going away from, so the letter for lake drops out

parts.note: a largo is a slow movement in music

explanation.surface: A mythical ship's stately progress away from a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'slow movement' is musical, not a ship's pace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship Jason and the Argonauts sailed in Greek myth.

clue.text: Copper's cat's habitual practice

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, with the S of the possessive
a tom is a male cat; the possessive 's is a link

explanation.surface: A policeman's pet has a routine habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is an established way of behaving, a habitual practice.

clue.text: Universal wit entertaining third of listeners

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the comedian's word takes the letter inside

parts.note: a wit is a comic

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of listeners

explanation.surface: A comedian with universal appeal, amusing a third of the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts S, the third letter of listeners, inside COMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic relates to the cosmos, the whole universe, so means universal.

clue.text: Virile army doctor ringing a key hospital

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the doctor surrounds the rest

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is an army doctor
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: A manly military medic phoning a major hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like phoning but encircles: MO goes around A, C and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes aggressive, showy masculinity, so it means virile.

clue.text: Most junior guy on set, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters of guy on set are rearranged

explanation.surface: The least senior chap on the film set, unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest is the one lowest in age, so the most junior.

clue.text: Faint, without disturbing younger family member

indicators.note: disturbing means breaking into, so the abbreviation goes inside the son

parts.note: a son is a younger member of a family
W/O, written WO, is short for without

explanation.surface: Passing out, without waking the youngest in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without disturbing' reads as 'without waking', but 'without' is W/O and 'disturbing' the insertion signal putting it inside SON.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, especially from strong emotion.

clue.text: Porter, say, primarily consuming Guinness?

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of consuming

explanation.surface: A dark beer, first and foremost, for anyone drinking stout like Guinness.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness is not the stout but the actor Sir Alec Guinness; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec is the first name of the actor Alec Guinness, so names a Guinness.

clue.text: Factory transformed into a cultivated area

parts.note: a plant is a factory

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters of into a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A factory converted into farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' scrambles only the word 'into'; the 'a' is taken as written and placed before those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation is an estate where crops such as tea or cotton are grown, a cultivated area.

clue.text: Right over the top, learner breaking the fuel regulator!

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the word the is split by the other pieces

parts.note: L, as on a learner driver's L-plate, stands for learner

explanation.surface: A learner driver going wildly overboard with the accelerator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the top' means excessive here, not a position above another piece; 'breaking' splits the word 'the' open.
explanation.definitionFit: A throttle is the valve controlling fuel flow to an engine, a fuel regulator.

clue.text: Mum meeting Granny? Any time will do

indicators.note: meeting means joining up with, so mum's word sits next to granny's

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
nana is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Mother meeting Grandma says the visit can be whenever suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, used to mean some unspecified later time, so 'any time will do'.
